conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I'll be taking care of you today. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I’ve been feeling dizzy and shaky since last night. My legs are tingling, and I feel weak. It’s happened before when my potassium gets too high.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense. You’re on dialysis, right? When was your last session?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’m on dialysis three times a week. My last one was two days ago. I know I should’ve gone yesterday, but I wasn’t feeling well and skipped it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That could explain it. We checked your labs in the ER, and your potassium was very high—6.9, which can be dangerous for the heart.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, that’s high. I remember feeling like this once before. Did you do an EKG?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your EKG was normal, which is a good sign. We gave you insulin, sugar, calcium, and albuterol to help bring the potassium down quickly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had that treatment before. It helps. Is my potassium better now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It came down to 6.6, but it’s still too high. You’ve already had one dialysis session since arriving. That should help a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, good. I feel a little less shaky now, but still tired.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s expected. We’ll keep an eye on you tonight. Your blood pressure and heart rate are stable, and your exam is normal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I didn’t have chest pain or shortness of breath, just the dizziness and tingling.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s reassuring. We’ll monitor you overnight. You’re not on telemetry right now because you’re stable, but we can adjust if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’d rather not be on it unless necessary. I’ve been on it before and it’s hard to sleep.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll respect that. Nurses will check on you regularly. We’ll also repeat your labs in the morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just checking in. How are you feeling now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better. The dizziness is gone. I had a small meal and some water. Still a bit weak, but not shaky anymore.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great progress. Your repeat potassium was 6.6 after the first dialysis, which is improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I might need another dialysis session?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. We’ll see what the morning labs show. The goal is to get your potassium under 5.5 before discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. I’ll stick to my diet better after this. No more bananas or oranges.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Your nephrologist will also review your dialysis schedule to prevent this from happening again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs came back. Your potassium is now 5.3—still a bit high, but much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: 5.3? Is that safe?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s in the high-normal range, but since you’ve had issues before, we want it lower. We’ve scheduled another 2.5-hour dialysis session today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I understand. After that, can I go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, likely. Once your potassium is stable and you’re feeling well, we’ll discharge you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I need to get back to my routine. What about my other meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All your regular medications are being continued—warfarin, lamotrigine, omeprazole, and the rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I didn’t bring my CPAP. Should I be using it here?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We can offer it, but since the masks don’t fit you well and you prefer not to, we’re holding it per your wishes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ll use it at home. Just not with the hospital ones.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You just finished your second dialysis session. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Tired, but okay. No dizziness or tingling. I think I’m ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your vitals are stable, and you’re alert and moving well. We’ll get your discharge papers ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need to check my potassium soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your nephrologist will check it at your next dialysis appointment. They may adjust your treatment plan.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll make sure to go to all my sessions. No more skipping.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s the best thing you can do. Keep taking your sevelamer and sodium polystyrene as prescribed to help control potassium.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for taking care of me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and call if you feel dizzy or unwell again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your discharge orders are in. You can leave once the nurse reviews your instructions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. I’ll pack up. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. Stay on top of your dialysis and diet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I’ve learned my lesson.
